title: Audit event index pruning & cost-aware ingestion pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce audit ingest and storage cost while preserving queryability and compliance guarantees for RBAC v2 / SSO/SAML sensitive events. This ticket implements an ingestion+indexing strategy that classifies events by retention tier, applies time-based pruning/rollups, and routes cold slices to object storage with searchable metadata.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingestion pipeline tags events with retention_tier (hot/standard/archival) based on event type and RBAC sensitivity rules; 2) Hot index provides <150ms median query for last 7 days; 3) Old indices beyond retention moved to S3 cold zone and replaceable by compacted rollup indices for basic audit queries; 4) Cost reduction target: 40% storage spend decrease for audit index cluster without losing required fields for compliance; 5) Admin console exposes retention controls per-organization and an override audit export flow.
design_decisions:
- Use Kafka topic with a lightweight enrichment step (ingest service) that annotates events with retention_tier and tenant labels.
- Maintain short-lived hot indices (daily) with ILM-style rollover and force-merge to optimize segment count.
- Implement periodic compaction job that generates time-windowed rollup docs for archival queries (counts, user/action counts) and expires raw events after archival TTL for non-sensitive types.
- Sensitive SSO/SAML and RBAC-v2 events are marked as immutable and stored in a cold-object-store backed index with cryptographic checksums to meet audit standards.
- Integrate with the RBAC v2 policy engine to decide retention tier at ingestion; default to longer retention for admin/privileged actions.
- Expose a cost-estimate API to the Console to show projected monthly storage by org and retention policy.
implementation_notes:
Ingest path: app -> kafka -> enrich-service (adds retention_tier) -> router -> write to elasticsearch cluster / object-store. Use timestamp-based partitioning: daily for hot, weekly for standard, monthly for archival manifests. Add bookkeeping index of archival manifests for search federation.
Indexing knobs: dynamic mappings limited to vetted schema; disallow arbitrary nested objects to control index bloat. Use shard sizing target 20-40GB; prefer fewer larger shards for cost efficiency.
Cost controls: enforce per-tenant retention defaults and hard caps via Quota service; auto-notify when projected storage exceeds threshold with suggestions (compress, shorten retention, enable rollup).
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Over-pruning could remove evidence needed for security investigations. Mitigation: flag critical event types (auth_failures, token_grants, role_changes) as immutable with explicit longer retention; add admin export before prune.
- Risk: Increased latency at write-time due to enrichment. Mitigation: make enrichment async if enrichment table misses; provide a fallback pipeline.
- Risk: Query patterns may break with rollups. Mitigation: provide transparent federated query layer that rewrites queries to consult rollup manifests and the cold store for older ranges.
updates: 2025-02-18: Scoped initial spike and validated event schema with Security team; identified ~25 event types needing extended retention.
2025-02-24: PoC ingest enrichment service implemented; added retention_tier field and tenant_id hashing. Latency median added ~6ms on ingestion path (acceptable).
2025-02-28: Architecture review with Infra and Security; decided on rollup strategy (daily->monthly) and cold CSV manifests for S3 retrieval. Action: Draft CLI export for auditors.
2025-03-03: Performance test on staging: hot index 7-day window median query 120ms for simple queries; complex aggregations need further optimization (cardinality heavy).
2025-03-05: Security requested cryptographic checksums for archival objects and proof-of-presence log; added to scope. Preparing PR for ILM policies and compaction job.
